QuestionStmt.S:
Identify the product 'X' formed in the following reaction,

Sodium ethoxide + Isopropyl chloride ⟶ X + Ethanol + Sodium chloride

Solution.S:
Sodium ethoxide (C₂H₅ONa) is a strong base and a good nucleophile. Isopropyl chloride ((CH₃)₂CHCl) is a secondary alkyl halide. In this reaction, sodium ethoxide attacks the carbon bearing the chlorine atom via an SN2 mechanism, displacing chloride and forming an ether. The product is 2-ethoxypropane (isopropyl ethyl ether). The reaction is:

$$\mathrm{CH_3CH_2ONa + (CH_3)_2CHCl \rightarrow (CH_3)_2CHOCH_2CH_3 + NaCl}$$

Thus the correct product is 2-ethoxypropane, which corresponds to option B.
